subject: Lifecycle cost restructure and escape credit query
messages:
From: Emma Carter <emma@dataforge.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lifecycle cost restructure and escape credit query

Hi Rishi / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the runtime performance looks promising. Before we escalate to our procurement team, we need a clearer read on two things that will determine whether we can match on price and operational risk:

1) Unbundling runtime vs. packaging: if we move to a smaller "runtime-only" SKU for inference (no managed data plane), what is the delta to your published package pricing? Please show both short-term pilot pricing and 12-month committed run-rates.

2) Escape / onboarding credits: our legal & procurement teams expect a clear escape-credit or rollback protection if we see a material performance delta after migration. What are Redwood's typical terms here (duration, token credit structure, and any limits tied to KV cache or burst usage)?

Attached is our internal procurement template (dataforge_po_template.docx) to speed review. Can you provide a concise price-bridge and a suggested pilot credit structure by EOW?

Appreciate it — we want to move fast if the economics line up.

Best,
Emma Carter
Head of Platform Partnerships
DataForge

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emma Carter <emma@dataforge.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lifecycle cost restructure and escape credit query

Emma — thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary below; I’ll follow up with a short spreadsheet (attached) that lays out the bridge between our standard package and a runtime-only SKU.

High-level answers:
- Runtime-only delta: roughly 25–35% lower base price for pure inference-only requests vs our full-managed package, depending on sequence length and KV cache hit rate. The attached model includes three traffic scenarios (pilot, steady-state, peak).
- Pilot pricing: we can do a 6-week pilot at a reduced committed rate (50% off published runtime MSRP for the pilot term) with a capped token allowance.
- Escape credits: standard is a 6-week credit window post-migration. If measured latency/regression exceeds agreed thresholds (99th percentile latency and quality baselines), we provide a pro-rated token credit covering 6 weeks of committed spend plus a one-time migration support credit. Credits exclude overage tokens tied to burst-only usage.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll attach the runbook_cost_model.xlsx with scenario tabs (Pilot / 6m / 12m).
2) Laura — can you add a brief ops note on what incompatibilities would prevent an escape-credit claim?
3) If this matches your ask, Emma — we’ll convert to a formal quote and provide a draft sideletter you can share with procurement.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lifecycle cost restructure and escape credit query

Emma — looping in Connor for the compatibility/ops specifics. A couple of clarifying points from an engineering perspective:

- What you call "runtime-only" typically implies you manage the model artifacts and the data plane; we still need to provide runtimes with KV-cache support and occasional software-level hotfixes. The main things that would invalidate an escape-credit claim are:
  * Changes to request patterns that trip sustained peak bursts (50%+ of pilot traffic sustained for >24 hours)
  * Manual config changes by your side that increase context window beyond the tested profile
  * Use of custom kernels/derivative model forks not covered in our compatibility matrix

- Deployment compatibility matrix is attached — it maps our runtime variants to common onboarding patterns and shows which items require a migration support ticket vs professional services (one-off).

On economics: we can propose a two-part construction for your pilot:
- A 6-week pilot at 50% off runtime MSRP (as Rishi mentioned) with a pilot token cap.
- If you sign a 12-month commit within 45 days after pilot close, we’ll extend a 20% committed discount for the first 3 months plus a one-time onboarding credit equal to 6 weeks of committed spend.

Connor — can you confirm the expected lead time for a canary rollout and whether a read-only KV-cache snapshot would be sufficient to validate performance?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with what procurement needs to see. A few quick items:

- The 6-week pilot at 50% + the onboarding credit sounds workable. Procurement wants the proposed sideletter language and a formal quote that calls out: pilot term, pilot token cap, the criteria that would trigger the escape-credit, and the mechanics for applying the credit on invoice.
- We can accept the 45-day conversion window.
- For the canary, a read-only KV-cache snapshot will be fine for initial validation. Connor, I’ll coordinate with your team on snapshot format & transfer.

Attached our PO template for legal redline. If you can send the DocuSign-ready quote & sideletter by Tue EOD (PST), we’ll route internally the following day. HubSpot deal HS-32451 is open if you want to link the quote.
